verses.english: Linked Discourses 48.41
5. Old Age
Old Age
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito pacchātape nisinno hoti piṭṭhiṁ otāpayamāno.
verses.english: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and sat warming his back in the last rays of the sun.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā bhagavato gattāni pāṇinā anomajjanto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and while massaging the Buddha’s limbs he said:
“It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing,

verses.pali: Na cevaṁ dāni, bhante, bhagavato tāva parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto, sithilāni ca gattāni sabbāni valiyajātāni, purato pabbhāro ca kāyo, dissati ca indriyānaṁ aññathattaṁ—
verses.english: how the complexion of your skin is no longer pure and bright. Your limbs are flaccid and wrinkled, and your body is stooped. And it’s apparent that there has been a deterioration in your faculties
of eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.”
“That’s how it is, Ānanda.

verses.pali: jarādhammo yobbaññe, byādhidhammo ārogye, maraṇadhammo jīvite.
verses.english: When young you’re liable to grow old; when healthy you’re liable to get sick; and when alive you’re liable to die.

verses.pali: Na ceva tāva parisuddho hoti chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto, sithilāni ca honti gattāni sabbāni valiyajātāni, purato pabbhāro ca kāyo, dissati ca indriyānaṁ aññathattaṁ—
verses.english: The complexion of the skin is no longer pure and bright. The limbs are flaccid and wrinkled, and the body is stooped. And it’s apparent that there has been a deterioration in the faculties
of eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.”
That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Idaṁ vatvā ca sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
verses.english: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Curse this wretched old age,
which makes you so ugly.
That’s how much this delightful puppet
is ground down by old age.
Even if you live for a hundred years,
you’ll still end up dying.
Death spares no-one,
but crushes all underfoot.”
